verses.original: δὲ Κατήντησεν καὶ εἰς Δέρβην καὶ εἰς Λύστραν καὶ ἐκεῖ ἦν ἰδοὺ τις μαθητής ὀνόματι Τιμόθεος υἱὸς πιστῆς Ἰουδαίας γυναικὸς δὲ Ἕλληνος πατρὸς
verses.transliteration: de Katēntēsen kai eis Derbēn kai eis Lystran kai ekei ēn idou tis mathētēs onomati Timotheos huios pistēs Ioudaias gynaikos de Hellēnos patros
verses.literal: - [Paul] came - to Derbe and then to Lystra - [where] - [he found] a disciple named Timothy [the] son of a believing Jewish woman and a Greek father

verses.original: τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἐν Λύστροις καὶ Ἰκονίῳ ἐμαρτυρεῖτο ὑπὸ ὃς
verses.transliteration: tōn adelphōn en Lystrois kai Ikoniō emartyreito hypo hos
verses.literal: The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of - [him]

verses.original: ὁ Παῦλος ἠθέλησεν τοῦτον ἐξελθεῖν σὺν αὐτῷ καὶ λαβὼν περιέτεμεν αὐτὸν διὰ τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τοὺς ὄντας ἐν ἐκείνοις τοῖς τόποις γὰρ ἅπαντες ᾔδεισαν ὅτι αὐτοῦ ὁ πατὴρ ὑπῆρχεν Ἕλλην
verses.transliteration: ho Paulos ēthelēsen touton exelthein syn autō kai labōn perietemen auton dia tous Ioudaious tous ontas en ekeinois tois topois gar hapantes ēdeisan hoti autou ho patēr hypērchen Hellēn
verses.literal: - Paul wanted [Timothy] to accompany . . . him [so] he took [him] [and] circumcised him on account of the Jews - - in that - area for vvv they all knew that his - father was a Greek

verses.original: δὲ Ὡς διεπορεύοντο τὰς πόλεις παρεδίδοσαν τὰ δόγματα τὰ κεκριμένα ὑπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων τῶν ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις αὐτοῖς φυλάσσειν
verses.transliteration: de Hōs dieporeuonto tas poleis paredidosan ta dogmata ta kekrimena hypo tōn apostolōn kai presbyterōn tōn en Hierosolymois autois phylassein
verses.literal: - As they went from - town to town they delivered the decisions - handed down by the apostles and elders - in Jerusalem for [the people] to obey

verses.original: οὖν μὲν Αἱ ἐκκλησίαι ἐστερεοῦντο τῇ πίστει καὶ ἐπερίσσευον καθ’ ἡμέραν τῷ ἀριθμῷ
verses.transliteration: oun men Hai ekklēsiai estereounto tē pistei kai eperisseuon kath’ hēmeran tō arithmō
verses.literal: So - the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew vvv daily - in numbers

verses.original: ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος κωλυθέντες λαλῆσαι τὸν λόγον ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ δὲ Διῆλθον τὴν χώραν Φρυγίαν καὶ Γαλατικὴν
verses.transliteration: hypo tou Hagiou Pneumatos kōlythentes lalēsai ton logon en tē Asia de Diēlthon tēn chōran Phrygian kai Galatikēn
verses.literal: - {After} the Holy Spirit had prevented them from speaking the word in - [the province of] Asia - they traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia

verses.original: δὲ ἐλθόντες κατὰ τὴν Μυσίαν ἐπείραζον πορευθῆναι εἰς τὴν Βιθυνίαν καὶ τὸ Πνεῦμα Ἰησοῦ οὐκ εἴασεν αὐτοὺς
verses.transliteration: de elthontes kata tēn Mysian epeirazon poreuthēnai eis tēn Bithynian kai to Pneuma Iēsou ouk eiasen autous
verses.literal: And when they came to the border of - Mysia they tried to enter . . . - Bithynia [but] the Spirit of Jesus vvv would not permit them

verses.original: δὲ παρελθόντες τὴν Μυσίαν κατέβησαν εἰς Τρῳάδα
verses.transliteration: de parelthontes tēn Mysian katebēsan eis Trōada
verses.literal: [So] they passed by - Mysia [and] went down to Troas

verses.original: Καὶ διὰ τῆς νυκτὸς τῷ Παύλῳ ὤφθη ὅραμα τις ἀνὴρ Μακεδών ἦν ἑστὼς καὶ παρακαλῶν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγων Διαβὰς εἰς Μακεδονίαν βοήθησον ἡμῖν
verses.transliteration: Kai dia tēs nyktos tō Paulō ōphthē horama tis anēr Makedōn ēn hestōs kai parakalōn auton kai legōn Diabas eis Makedonian boēthēson hēmin
verses.literal: - During the night - Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia - standing and pleading with him - - Come over to Macedonia [and] help us

verses.original: δὲ ὡς εἶδεν τὸ ὅραμα ἐζητήσαμεν εὐθέως ἐξελθεῖν εἰς Μακεδονίαν συμβιβάζοντες ὅτι ὁ Θεὸς προσκέκληται ἡμᾶς εὐαγγελίσασθαι αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: de hōs eiden to horama ezētēsamen eutheōs exelthein eis Makedonian symbibazontes hoti ho Theos proskeklētai hēmas euangelisasthai autous
verses.literal: - As soon as [Paul] had seen the vision we got ready - to leave for Macedonia concluding that - God had called us to preach the gospel to them

verses.original: δὲ Ἀναχθέντες ἀπὸ Τρῳάδος εὐθυδρομήσαμεν εἰς Σαμοθρᾴκην δὲ τῇ ἐπιούσῃ εἰς Νέαν Πόλιν
verses.transliteration: de Anachthentes apo Trōados euthydromēsamen eis Samothrakēn de tē epiousē eis Nean Polin
verses.literal: - We sailed from Troas straight to Samothrace and the following day on to Neapolis . . .

verses.original: κἀκεῖθεν εἰς κολωνία Φιλίππους ἥτις ἐστὶν πρώτη πόλις τῆς μερίδος Μακεδονίας δὲ Ἦμεν διατρίβοντες ἐν ταύτῃ τῇ πόλει τινάς ἡμέρας
verses.transliteration: kakeithen eis kolōnia Philippous hētis estin prōtē polis tēs meridos Makedonias de Ēmen diatribontes en tautē tē polei tinas hēmeras
verses.literal: From there [we went] to [the Roman] colony of Philippi - - [the] leading city of [that] district of Macedonia And vvv we stayed vvv vvv vvv [there] [several] days

verses.original: τε Τῇ τῶν σαββάτων ἡμέρᾳ ἐξήλθομεν ἔξω τῆς πύλης παρὰ ποταμὸν οὗ ἐνομίζομεν εἶναι προσευχὴν καὶ καθίσαντες ἐλαλοῦμεν ταῖς γυναιξίν συνελθούσαις
verses.transliteration: te Tē tōn sabbatōn hēmera exēlthomen exō tēs pylēs para potamon hou enomizomen einai proseuchēn kai kathisantes elaloumen tais gynaixin synelthousais
verses.literal: - On the - Sabbath . . . we went outside the city gate along [the] river where [it] was customary to find [a place of] prayer [After] sitting down we spoke to the women who had gathered [there]

verses.original: Καί ἤκουεν τις γυνὴ ὀνόματι Λυδία πορφυρόπωλις πόλεως Θυατείρων σεβομένη τὸν Θεόν ὁ Κύριος διήνοιξεν ἧς τὴν καρδίαν προσέχειν τοῖς ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου λαλουμένοις
verses.transliteration: Kai ēkouen tis gynē onomati Lydia porphyropōlis poleōs Thyateirōn sebomenē ton Theon ho Kyrios diēnoixen hēs tēn kardian prosechein tois hypo tou Paulou laloumenois
verses.literal: - Among those listening [was] a woman named Lydia a dealer in purple [cloth] from [the] city of Thyatira [who was] a worshiper of God The Lord opened her - heart to respond to - - Paul’s message

verses.original: δὲ ὡς καὶ αὐτῆς ὁ οἶκος ἐβαπτίσθη παρεκάλεσεν λέγουσα Εἰ κεκρίκατέ με εἶναι πιστὴν τῷ Κυρίῳ εἰσελθόντες μένετε εἰς μου τὸν οἶκόν καὶ παρεβιάσατο ἡμᾶς
verses.transliteration: de hōs kai autēs ho oikos ebaptisthē parekalesen legousa Ei kekrikate me einai pistēn tō Kyriō eiselthontes menete eis mou ton oikon kai parebiasato hēmas
verses.literal: And when [she] and her - household had been baptized she urged [us] . . . If you consider me vvv a believer in the Lord come [and] stay at my - house And she persuaded us

verses.original: δὲ Ἐγένετο ἡμῶν πορευομένων εἰς τὴν προσευχὴν ἡμῖν ὑπαντῆσαι τινὰ παιδίσκην ἔχουσαν πνεῦμα Πύθωνα ἥτις παρεῖχεν πολλὴν ἐργασίαν αὐτῆς τοῖς κυρίοις μαντευομένη
verses.transliteration: de Egeneto hēmōn poreuomenōn eis tēn proseuchēn hēmin hypantēsai tina paidiskēn echousan pneuma Pythōna hētis pareichen pollēn ergasian autēs tois kyriois manteuomenē
verses.literal: One day . . . as we were going to the [place of] prayer we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination who earned a large income for her - masters by fortune-telling

verses.original: αὕτη κατακολουθοῦσα τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ἡμῖν ἔκραζεν λέγουσα Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἰσίν δοῦλοι τοῦ τοῦ Ὑψίστου Θεοῦ οἵτινες καταγγέλλουσιν ὑμῖν ὁδὸν σωτηρίας
verses.transliteration: hautē katakolouthousa tō Paulō kai hēmin ekrazen legousa Houtoi hoi anthrōpoi eisin douloi tou tou Hypsistou Theou hoitines katangellousin hymin hodon sōtērias
verses.literal: [This girl] followed - Paul and [the rest of] us shouting . . . These - men are servants of the - Most High God who are proclaiming to you [the] way of salvation

verses.original: δὲ ἐποίει Τοῦτο ἐπὶ πολλὰς ἡμέρας δὲ Παῦλος διαπονηθεὶς καὶ ἐπιστρέψας εἶπεν τῷ πνεύματι ἐν ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ Παραγγέλλω σοι ἐξελθεῖν ἀπ’ αὐτῆς καὶ ἐξῆλθεν αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ
verses.transliteration: de epoiei Touto epi pollas hēmeras de Paulos diaponētheis kai epistrepsas eipen tō pneumati en onomati Iēsou Christou Parangellō soi exelthein ap’ autēs kai exēlthen autē tē hōra
verses.literal: - She continued this for many days [Eventually] Paul grew so aggravated [that] he turned [and] said to the spirit In [the] name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her And [the spirit] left her at that - very moment

verses.original: δὲ αὐτῆς οἱ κύριοι Ἰδόντες ὅτι αὐτῶν ἡ ἐλπὶς τῆς ἐργασίας ἐξῆλθεν ἐπιλαβόμενοι τὸν Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἵλκυσαν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἄρχοντας εἰς τὴν ἀγορὰν
verses.transliteration: de autēs hoi kyrioi Idontes hoti autōn hē elpis tēs ergasias exēlthen epilabomenoi ton Paulon kai ton Silan heilkysan epi tous archontas eis tēn agoran
verses.literal: [When] [the girl’s] - owners saw that their - hope of making money was gone they seized - Paul and - Silas [and] dragged [them] before the authorities in the marketplace

verses.original: καὶ προσαγαγόντες αὐτοὺς τοῖς στρατηγοῖς εἶπαν Οὗτοι οἱ ἄνθρωποι ὑπάρχοντες Ἰουδαῖοι ἐκταράσσουσιν ἡμῶν τὴν πόλιν
verses.transliteration: kai prosagagontes autous tois stratēgois eipan Houtoi hoi anthrōpoi hyparchontes Ioudaioi ektarassousin hēmōn tēn polin
verses.literal: - They brought them . . . to the magistrates [and] said These - men are Jews [and] are throwing our - city {into turmoil}

verses.original: καὶ καταγγέλλουσιν ἔθη ἃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν ἡμῖν οὖσιν Ῥωμαίοις παραδέχεσθαι οὐδὲ ποιεῖν
verses.transliteration: kai katangellousin ethē ha ouk exestin hēmin ousin Rhōmaiois paradechesthai oude poiein
verses.literal: [by] promoting customs that vvv are unlawful for us - Romans to adopt [or] practice

verses.original: Καὶ ὁ ὄχλος συνεπέστη κατ’ αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ στρατηγοὶ ἐκέλευον περιρήξαντες αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ῥαβδίζειν
verses.transliteration: Kai ho ochlos synepestē kat’ autōn kai hoi stratēgoi ekeleuon perirēxantes autōn ta himatia rhabdizein
verses.literal: - The crowd joined in the attack against [Paul and Silas] and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped . . . . . . . . . [and] beaten with rods

verses.original: τε ἐπιθέντες αὐτοῖς πολλάς πληγὰς ἔβαλον εἰς φυλακήν παραγγείλαντες τῷ δεσμοφύλακι τηρεῖν αὐτούς ἀσφαλῶς
verses.transliteration: te epithentes autois pollas plēgas ebalon eis phylakēn parangeilantes tō desmophylaki tērein autous asphalōs
verses.literal: And after striking them with many blows they threw [them] into prison [and] ordered the jailer to guard them securely

verses.original: ὃς λαβὼν τοιαύτην παραγγελίαν ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν ἐσωτέραν φυλακὴν καὶ ἠσφαλίσατο αὐτῶν τοὺς πόδας εἰς τὸ ξύλον
verses.transliteration: hos labōn toiautēn parangelian ebalen autous eis tēn esōteran phylakēn kai ēsphalisato autōn tous podas eis to xylon
verses.literal: - On receiving [this] order he placed them in the inner cell and fastened their - feet in the stocks

verses.original: δὲ Κατὰ τὸ μεσονύκτιον Παῦλος καὶ Σιλᾶς προσευχόμενοι ὕμνουν τὸν Θεόν δὲ οἱ δέσμιοι ἐπηκροῶντο αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: de Kata to mesonyktion Paulos kai Silas proseuchomenoi hymnoun ton Theon de hoi desmioi epēkroōnto autōn
verses.literal: - About - midnight Paul and Silas were praying [and] singing hymns to God and the [other] prisoners were listening to them

verses.original: δὲ ἄφνω ἐγένετο μέγας σεισμὸς ὥστε σαλευθῆναι τὰ θεμέλια τοῦ δεσμωτηρίου δὲ παραχρῆμα πᾶσαι αἱ θύραι ἠνεῴχθησαν καὶ πάντων τὰ δεσμὰ ἀνέθη
verses.transliteration: de aphnō egeneto megas seismos hōste saleuthēnai ta themelia tou desmōtēriou de parachrēma pasai hai thyrai ēneōchthēsan kai pantōn ta desma anethē
verses.literal: vvv Suddenly - a strong earthquake - shook the foundations of the prison - At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s - chains came loose

verses.original: δὲ ὁ δεσμοφύλαξ γενόμενος Ἔξυπνος καὶ ἰδὼν τὰς τῆς φυλακῆς θύρας ἀνεῳγμένας σπασάμενος τὴν μάχαιραν ἤμελλεν ἀναιρεῖν ἑαυτὸν νομίζων τοὺς δεσμίους ἐκπεφευγέναι
verses.transliteration: de ho desmophylax genomenos Exypnos kai idōn tas tēs phylakēs thyras aneōgmenas spasamenos tēn machairan ēmellen anairein heauton nomizōn tous desmious ekpepheugenai
verses.literal: [When] the jailer vvv woke up and saw the - prison doors open he drew his sword [and] was about to kill himself presuming that the prisoners had escaped

verses.original: δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἐφώνησεν μεγάλῃ φωνῇ λέγων πράξῃς Μηδὲν κακόν σεαυτῷ γάρ ἐσμεν ἅπαντες ἐνθάδε
verses.transliteration: de ho Paulos ephōnēsen megalē phōnē legōn praxēs Mēden kakon seautō gar esmen hapantes enthade
verses.literal: But - Paul called out in a loud voice - Do not harm yourself - We are all here

verses.original: δὲ Αἰτήσας φῶτα εἰσεπήδησεν καὶ γενόμενος προσέπεσεν ἔντρομος τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Σιλᾷ
verses.transliteration: de Aitēsas phōta eisepēdēsen kai genomenos prosepesen entromos tō Paulō kai tō Sila
verses.literal: - Calling for lights [the jailer] rushed in and vvv fell trembling {before} - Paul and - Silas

verses.original: καὶ προαγαγὼν αὐτοὺς ἔξω ἔφη Κύριοι τί δεῖ με ποιεῖν ἵνα σωθῶ
verses.transliteration: kai proagagōn autous exō ephē Kyrioi ti dei me poiein hina sōthō
verses.literal: Then he brought them out [and] asked Sirs what must I do to be saved

verses.original: δὲ Οἱ εἶπαν Πίστευσον ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν καὶ σωθήσῃ σὺ καὶ σου ὁ οἶκός
verses.transliteration: de Hoi eipan Pisteuson epi ton Kyrion Iēsoun kai sōthēsē sy kai sou ho oikos
verses.literal: - - They replied Believe in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved you and your - household

verses.original: καὶ ἐλάλησαν τὸν λόγον τοῦ κυρίου αὐτῷ σὺν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἐν αὐτοῦ τῇ οἰκίᾳ
verses.transliteration: kai elalēsan ton logon tou kyriou autō syn pasin tois en autou tē oikia
verses.literal: Then [Paul and Silas] spoke the word of the Lord to him [and] to everyone . . . in his - house

verses.original: καὶ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ τῆς νυκτὸς παραλαβὼν αὐτοὺς ἔλουσεν ἀπὸ τῶν πληγῶν καὶ παραχρῆμα αὐτὸς καὶ πάντες αὐτοῦ οἱ ἐβαπτίσθη
verses.transliteration: kai en ekeinē tē hōra tēs nyktos paralabōn autous elousen apo tōn plēgōn kai parachrēma autos kai pantes autou hoi ebaptisthē
verses.literal: - At that - hour of the night [the jailer] took them [and] washed - [their] wounds And without delay he and all his household were baptized

verses.original: τε ἀναγαγών αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν οἶκον παρέθηκεν τράπεζαν καὶ πανοικεὶ ἠγαλλιάσατο πεπιστευκὼς τῷ Θεῷ
verses.transliteration: te anagagōn autous eis ton oikon parethēken trapezan kai panoikei ēgalliasato pepisteukōs tō Theō
verses.literal: Then he brought them into [his] home and set [a meal before them] [So] {he} and all [his] household rejoiced that they had come to believe - in God

verses.original: δὲ Ἡμέρας γενομένης οἱ στρατηγοὶ ἀπέστειλαν τοὺς ῥαβδούχους λέγοντες Ἀπόλυσον ἐκείνους τοὺς ἀνθρώπους
verses.transliteration: de Hēmeras genomenēs hoi stratēgoi apesteilan tous rhabdouchous legontes Apolyson ekeinous tous anthrōpous
verses.literal: [When] daylight came the magistrates sent [their] officers with the order Release those - men

verses.original: δὲ ὁ δεσμοφύλαξ Ἀπήγγειλεν τούτους τοὺς λόγους πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον ὅτι οἱ στρατηγοὶ Ἀπέσταλκαν ἵνα ἀπολυθῆτε οὖν νῦν ἐξελθόντες πορεύεσθε ἐν εἰρήνῃ
verses.transliteration: de ho desmophylax Apēngeilen toutous tous logous pros ton Paulon hoti hoi stratēgoi Apestalkan hina apolythēte oun nyn exelthontes poreuesthe en eirēnē
verses.literal: - The jailer informed . . . . . . . . . . . . - Paul - The magistrates have sent orders to release you - Now vvv you may go on your way in peace

verses.original: δὲ Ὁ Παῦλος ἔφη πρὸς αὐτούς Δείραντες ἡμᾶς δημοσίᾳ ἀκατακρίτους ἀνθρώπους ἔβαλαν εἰς φυλακήν ὑπάρχοντας Ῥωμαίους καὶ νῦν ἐκβάλλουσιν ἡμᾶς λάθρᾳ οὐ γάρ ἀλλὰ ἐλθόντες αὐτοὶ ἐξαγαγέτωσαν ἡμᾶς
verses.transliteration: de Ho Paulos ephē pros autous Deirantes hēmas dēmosia akatakritous anthrōpous ebalan eis phylakēn hyparchontas Rhōmaious kai nyn ekballousin hēmas lathra ou gar alla elthontes autoi exagagetōsan hēmas
verses.literal: But - Paul said to [the officers] They beat us publicly without a trial . . . [and] threw [us] into prison [even though] we are Roman citizens And now do they want to send us away . . . secretly Absolutely not . . . . . . Let them come themselves and escort us out . . .

verses.original: δὲ οἱ ῥαβδοῦχοι Ἀπήγγειλαν ταῦτα τὰ ῥήματα τοῖς στρατηγοῖς δὲ ἐφοβήθησαν ἀκούσαντες ὅτι εἰσιν Ῥωμαῖοί
verses.transliteration: de hoi rhabdouchoi Apēngeilan tauta ta rhēmata tois stratēgois de ephobēthēsan akousantes hoti eisin Rhōmaioi
verses.literal: [So] the officers relayed this - message to the magistrates [who] were alarmed to hear that [Paul and Silas] were Roman citizens

verses.original: καὶ ἐλθόντες παρεκάλεσαν αὐτούς καὶ ἐξαγαγόντες ἠρώτων ἀπελθεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς πόλεως
verses.transliteration: kai elthontes parekalesan autous kai exagagontes ērōtōn apelthein apo tēs poleōs
verses.literal: - They came to appease them and led them out requesting that they leave . . . the city

verses.original: δὲ ἐξελθόντες ἀπὸ τῆς φυλακῆς εἰσῆλθον πρὸς τὴν Λυδίαν καὶ ἰδόντες τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς παρεκάλεσαν καὶ ἐξῆλθαν
verses.transliteration: de exelthontes apo tēs phylakēs eisēlthon pros tēn Lydian kai idontes tous adelphous parekalesan kai exēlthan
verses.literal: - After [Paul and Silas] came out of the prison they went to vvv Lydia’s house - to see the brothers and encourage [them] Then they left [ the city ]
